sentences.text:
THIS WRIT PETITION COMING ON FOR PRELIMINARY HEARING IN 'B' GROUP, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER

The petitioner has sought for issuance of appropriate writ, order or direction to the respondents to notify the land of petitioner measuring 3 Acres comprised in Block No.7, Sy.No.7 of B.K.Palya, Jala Hobli, Yelahanka Taluk, Bangalore Urban District.
It is submitted that the land may be notified for the benefit of KIADB and market value may be fixed.

2. It is the case of the petitioner that petitioner is the owner of an extent of 3 Acres of land in Sy.No.7, situated at Bandi Kodigehallipalya (B.K.Palya), Jala Hobli, Yelahanka Taluk, Bangalore Urban District.

It is submitted that the revenue records stand in the name of the NC:
2023:KHC:20301 petitioner till 2008 and subsequently, the Record of Rights also stand in the name of the petitioner.
3.

It is submitted that the land of the petitioner came to be notified for acquisition and notifications under Section 3 (1) and 1 (3) of KIAD Act has been passed.
4.

It is submitted that as certain questions regarding the validity of Grant Certificate were raised, the Special Deputy Commissioner in RRT(2) N(A)/CR-02/ 2021-22 in exercise of power under Section 136 (3) of the Karnataka Land Revenue Act held an enquiry and concluded that an extent of 3 Acres in Sy.No.7, situated at B.K.Palya Village, Jala Hobli, Yelahanka Taluk was legal entitlement of the petitioner by virtue of land grant and direction was issued to the Tahsildar to take necessary steps to mutate and continue the name of the petitioner herein in the revenue records to an extent of 3 Acres in Sy.No.7 as referred to above.
The order of 11.01.2022 in exercise of power under Section 136 (3) of the Act has attained finality.

It is submitted that since prior to the order of the Special Deputy Commissioner the entries were in the name of the Government, the Government is stated to have passed an order directing the KIADB to deposit the market value of the land as is evidenced from Annexure-R2 dated 29.04.2015.
On 16.05.2015, lands came to be handed over to the Special Land Acquisition Officer, KIADB by the Tahsildar.

It is the case made out on behalf of the petitioner that in light of her right and entitlement having been recognized by the order of the Special Deputy Commissioner under Section 136 (3)
proceedings, which however came to be disposed off only on 11.01.2021, she is entitled for compensation with respect to the land, entries of which were restored in the name of private land owners only after the order of 136 (3).
6. Attention is drawn to the order of the Coordinate Bench in W.P.Nos.51524-51525/2017 wherein this court after consideration of similar factual matrix has disposed NC: 2023:KHC:20301 off the Smt Saraswathamma vs State Of Karnataka on 13 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14430946/
3 petition directing the State Government to refund and remit back the amount deposited by the KIADB as would cover the claim of the petitioners and there upon respondent-KIADB has been directed to take steps for disbursing compensation to the petitioners/land losers as per the procedure under law after ascertaining their credentials.
7.

It is pointed out that the Coordinate Bench had also observed that it is open for the KIADB and its SLAO to solicit any information/copies of documents from the side of petitioners as are required for considering settlement of claim/compensation.
8. Insofar as interest on the said amount as asserted by the learned counsel for petitioner

, attention is drawn to the order in W.P.No.46860/2018 disposed off on 12.04.2022 wherein an identical factual matrix raising similar questions, the writ petition came to be disposed off directing the Special Land Acquisition Officer, KIADB to pay interest to the petitioners at 9% per annum from the NC: 2023:KHC:20301 date on which possession of the property was taken till the date of disbursal of compensation.

8. Though learned counsel Sri.P.V.Chandrashekar has raised various contentions and also contends that compensation is not required to be paid and question of payment of interest, which liability is imposed on KIADB is impermissible in law.

However, taking note of the order passed by the Coordinate Bench on identical factual matrix, the contentions are rejected and the order is passed as made in W.P.Nos.51524-51525/2017 and W.P.No.46860/2018.

9. It is further pointed out that the rate of compensation as regards other similarly placed land losers has been noticed in W.P.No.46860/2018 and the compensation of Rs.62 Lakhs per acre has been awarded.

10. Taking note of the orders passed in W.P.Nos.51524-525/2017 and W.P.No.46860/2018, the writ petition has to be allowed on the following terms:
NC: 2023:KHC:20301 i) Respondent nos.1 and 5 are to ensure that amount of compensation at Rs.62 Lakhs per acre compensated by KIADB as is evidenced from Annexure-R2 to be deposited to the respondent no.3, SLAO, KIADB.
ii) Upon such deposit to be made within a period of two months from the date of receipt of certified copy of the order, the 3rd respondent to disburse the amount to the petitioner after verifying necessary records and calling upon the petitioner to follow the procedure for the purpose of disbursal of compensation.
iii) KIADB is required to pay interest at 9% per annum from the date of taking possession i.e., from 16.06.2015 till the date of disbursal of compensation.
It is made clear that the amount of compensation that is being paid by the KIADB is to be construed as payment of compensation under the agreement under Section 29 (2).

However, it is made clear that this would not in any way interfere with compliance of the directions by the KIADB vis--vis the petitioner.
v) KIADB to pay the amount with interest to the petitioner in terms of the above directions within a period of two months from the date of receipt of amount from the Tahsildar/State Government.
Accordingly, the petition is disposed off.
However, it is made clear that the order is passed on the peculiar facts and circumstances of the case and is confined to dispute in relation to Sy.No.7.
The legal questions not adjudicated upon are kept open to be considered in other matters.
